# Vendored: github.com/full-chaos/atlassian (go/ directory)

Source: https://github.com/full-chaos/atlassian at cb7c3665cb90 (2026-07-16).
Copied from upstream: go/go.mod, go/atlassian/ (the Go module's library tree), LICENSE; modified ONLY by the patches listed under "Local modifications" below. Tests and tools directories are not copied.

Why vendored: the upstream go.mod declares `module atlassian`, which the Go proxy refuses when fetched as
github.com/full-chaos/atlassian/go. Ops requires it as `atlassian` and points it here with a replace directive.
Replace this directory with a normal tagged require once upstream declares its real module path.

Location: the path contains a `vendor` element on purpose: ci/check_go.sh skips `*/vendor/*` when it discovers Go
modules and when it checks formatting, so third-party code is neither vetted nor gofmt-checked as ops code. The root
module reaches it only through the replace directive in go.mod.

## Local modifications

`UPSTREAM.sha256` holds one sha256 per upstream file (from a clone of the commit above). `TestVendoredTreeIsUpstreamPlusExactlyTheRecordedPatches` reverses every patch, newest first, from this tree and requires the pinned upstream tree back, and requires one table row below per patch file. A change with no patch, a patch with no change, or a missing row fails it.

A re-vendor must re-apply these, or drop one only when upstream carries the same change. Each patch is a
unified diff against the upstream text at the commit above, in `patches/`; the tests that keep the changes from
silently regressing is `internal/atlassianteams/vendored_documents_test.go` (it reads every document of
`atlassian/graph` and `atlassian/graph/gen` and fails on the conflict below).

| patch | file | upstream text | our text | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `patches/0001-alias-typed-cypher-values.patch` (CHAOS-7493) | `atlassian/graph/gen/teamwork_graph_api.go` (the five Teamwork Graph documents `TEAMWORKGRAPH_TEAMACTIVEPROJECTS`, `_TEAMUSERS`, `_USERTEAMS`, `_USERMANAGER`, `_USERDIRECTREPORTS`, and the decoders of the typed value objects) | `... on GraphStoreCypherQueryV2StringObject { value }`, `... on GraphStoreCypherQueryV2IntObject { value }`, and the Float, Boolean and Timestamp objects likewise: one response key, `value`, selected with a different scalar type under each fragment; decoders read `json:"value"` | the same fragments with aliases: `{ stringValue: value }`, `{ intValue: value }`, `{ floatValue: value }`, `{ booleanValue: value }`, `{ timestampValue: value }`; decoders read `json:"stringValue"` etc.; the decoder's untyped fallback probes `stringValue` | The Atlassian gateway refuses the upstream documents with `Validation error (FieldsConflict) : '.../columns/value/value' : returns different types 'String' and 'Int'` (GraphQL "fields can merge": one response key with different types across fragments). Found by running `dho sync teams --provider jira` against the live gateway: every members read failed, so the Atlassian Teams sync wrote nothing. |
| `patches/0002-operation-names-match-documents.patch` (CHAOS-7132; a unified diff against the text after patch 0001) | `atlassian/graph/teamwork_graph.go` (the five Execute / ExecuteWithExtraHeaders calls of the Teamwork Graph reads) | operationName `"TeamworkGraph_teamUsers"`, `"TeamworkGraph_teamActiveProjects"`, `"TeamworkGraph_userTeams"`, `"TeamworkGraph_userManager"`, `"TeamworkGraph_userDirectReports"` | `"TeamworkGraphTeamUsers"`, `"TeamworkGraphTeamActiveProjects"`, `"TeamworkGraphUserTeams"`, `"TeamworkGraphUserManager"`, `"TeamworkGraphUserDirectReports"` (the query names the documents of `gen/teamwork_graph_api.go` declare) | The live gateway answers `Unknown operation named 'TeamworkGraph_teamUsers'` when operationName is not a query name of the document sent. Found by the live `dho sync teams --provider jira` rerun after patch 0001. Kept from regressing by `TestEveryVendoredExecuteCallNamesAnOperationItsDocumentDeclares`. |

Only the calls a caller marks send it (`internal/atlassianteams.Collect` marks the members read) |
| `patches/0004-team-members-take-the-requested-team-when-the-row-has-no-team-column.patch` (CHAOS-7902; against the text after patch 0003) | `atlassian/graph/teamwork_graph.go` (IterTeamUsers) and the new file `atlassian/graph/mappers/team_member.go` | IterTeamUsers maps each row with `TeamworkUserRelationFromGraphQL(node, "TEAM_MEMBER", "")`, which refuses a row with no team node ("TEAM_MEMBER relation requires team node") | IterTeamUsers maps each row with `TeamMemberRelationForTeam(node, teamID)`: the member is the row's user and the team is the row's team node when it has one, else the team id the read asked for; a row with no user is still refused, and so is a row whose explicit team node has a blank id ("team.id is required", as before) | the live gateway answers the team-users read with ONE column per edge, the user (a structure-only probe of 2026-10-02: `user` / GraphStoreCypherQueryV2AriNode / AtlassianAccountUser, no team column); the team is the request's variable. Found by the live `dho sync teams --provider jira` rerun after patch 0003. Kept from regressing by `TestCollectReadsMembersFromEdgesThatCarryOnlyTheUser` |
| `patches/0005-default-http-clients-follow-no-redirect.patch` (CHAOS-7921; against the text after patch 0004) | the new file `atlassian/default_http_client.go` and the 8 default-client sites: `atlassian/graph/client.go` (Execute, ExecuteWithExtraHeaders), `atlassian/graph/schema_fetcher.go` (FetchSchemaIntrospection), `atlassian/oauth_3lo.go` (postOAuthToken, FetchAccessibleResources), `atlassian/rest/client.go` (GetJSON, requestJSON, Delete) | each site built `&http.Client{Timeout: ...}` when its caller supplied no client: a client that follows up to ten redirects and re-sends custom headers to a new host | each site builds `NewDefaultHTTPClient(timeout)`: the same timeout and `CheckRedirect` = `http.ErrUseLastResponse` (a 3xx is returned as the response, nothing is followed) | production supplies its own guarded client, so the default only matters when none is supplied; a credential must not follow a redirect to another host (CHAOS-7910 class). Kept from regressing by `TestEveryVendoredHTTPClientRefusesRedirects` (the http.Client literals and default-client sites are DERIVED from the vendored source; empty = fail; the sites must equal the behaviour table) and `TestVendoredDefaultClientsFollowNoRedirect` (every site: the second host sees 0 requests) |

The team search left out a team with no member unless `showEmptyTeams: true` was sent, and that team had a connected project. The document selects fields under the `JiraProject` arm only, so it adds no cross-fragment field overlap. Kept from regressing by `TestConnectedContainersReadThroughTheRealClient` and `TestTheTeamSearchAsksForEmptyTeams` (`internal/atlassianteams`) |

A `nodes` list that is there and empty with `pageInfo.hasNextPage: false` is still a valid empty answer | the caller (`internal/atlassianteams`) takes the returned list for the WHOLE list and retracts what is not in it: a search answer with no `pageInfo` that listed 1 of 3 teams deactivated 2 teams and closed their ownership rows (reproduced against a real ClickHouse on the tip before this patch). An answer that does not say where its list ends, or does not carry the list, is not an empty last page. Kept from regressing by `TestTheTeamSearchDecoderRefusesAnAnswerWithAMissingPart`, `TestATeamSearchAnswerWithAMissingPartIsAFailedSearch` and `TestALinkTheProviderStillReturnsIsNeverClosed` (`internal/atlassianteams`); the `edges` half of the same rule is in patch 0006 (`TestTheLinkDecoderRefusesAnAnswerWithAMissingPart`, `TestALinkAnswerWithNoListOfLinksIsAFailedRead`) |

A stated `pageInfo.hasNextPage: false` is the end of the roster. NOT changed here: a missing or null `edges` list on a stated last page is still read as zero members, because no recorded real answer of an empty roster says whether the provider sends an empty list or null for it | the caller (`internal/atlassianteams`) takes the result for the whole roster of the team and closes the memberships the answer does not carry, so an answer that does not state its end must fail the member read, not read as the last page (the page-end half of the rule patches 0006 and 0007 give the link read and the team search). Kept from regressing by `TestTheTeamUsersDecoderRefusesAnAnswerWithoutAStatedPageEnd`, `TestAMemberReadWithoutAStatedPageEndIsAFailedCollection` and `TestAMemberReadWithoutAProvenEndClosesNoMembership` (`internal/atlassianteams`) |
